body: The string delimiter system is independent from the characters, so `"` and `'` should not be hardcoded in CodeEdit.

This doesn't consider if the comment is not a single line comment. Like `/* */` (in shader text editor).
Or if the comment marker is in a string I think.
It seems this can't fully rely on the existing delimiter checking system, so its duplicating a lot of logic like checking if it is in a string manually multiple times.
Youre right, it should probably use the `has_string_delimiter()` function. Another downside is that it doesnt check for multi-character string delimiters
Good catch! It should skip checking anything inside single line comments in addition to strings instead of breaking early when encountering a comment

Its not exactly checking if its *in* a string. It just checks if a string started, then skips doing other checks until it has reached the end of the string before resuming. It should however also check if a single line comment started and skip that too
